_note: Pilot assumptions from HiveMind.docx. Every number here is a starting point to tune, not a validated finding.

success._bandNote: A topic that is tiny at baseline must grow more (3x) to count as a hit than a large one (1.5x); at least minPeakStories stories at the peak.

topics._note: A topic must be covered by at least this many independent origins to rank. Vague filler labels are hidden from rankings (not deleted).

hot._note: Hot topics get a wider web check (Serper news search) and, within budget, a search-interest fetch. Budgets are per calendar day.

fulltext._note: Second attempts at articles that were only read from the headline. Fetched directly (the proxy adds nothing for article pages) and re-read once; the earlier reading is kept.

seasonality._note: Weekday adjustment switches on once there are this many days of history.

tuning._note: Weights are only re-tuned from measured outcomes once there are enough of them.

pricing._note: Optional: price per million tokens, to show an estimated spend. Leave empty to show tokens only.

openai._note: GPT-5.6 Luna, list price per million tokens (cached input is 0.02).

groq._note: gpt-oss-120b list price per million tokens; check Groq's pricing page, it may have changed.

reading._note: Stories are read from the headline and snippet only (set HIVEMIND_FULLTEXT=1 to fetch article text again). This cuts model cost; the evidence rules therefore lean on independent origins, not on full-text share.
reading._fullTextNote: "after": stories are first read from headlines (Claude), then the full-text job re-reads their articles with the low-cost model, keeping topic labels, to add detail. Measured: the low-cost model's own topic labels agreed only ~27-37% with Claude's, so it never assigns topics.

titlePatterns: OTT releases? this week|Web series to watch
junk._note: Template pages (topic landing pages, scoreboards) that are not news: skipped at collection and excluded from analysis.

batchApi._note: Backlogs of at least this many items use the discounted batch service (results within hours) instead of live calls.

topicVerify._note: Headlines filed under the topics behind today's opportunities are checked against the topic; those that do not fit are left out (reversibly).

angleFit._note: Second check in the same job as topicVerify: each topic's recent headlines are checked against the topic's best angle (not just the topic name). Headlines that do not support the angle are left out of that topic (reversibly). At most maxTopics x maxPerTopic headlines in a pass, Groq only, each headline checked once per angle.

online._note: Online opinion/analysis pieces. countInHeadroom: they are added to the print count in the headroom. sections: the newspapers' opinion pages are polled (free, no model) and the stories found there are marked opinion. sectionRead: also read the opinion-page stories that were not collected otherwise (adds model cost, off). analyze: after each collection read the text of up to dailyCap pieces, confirm the label, find the writer and match the angle (Groq, off by default; the Leadership page has a button for one run).

ocr._note: Print editions from the OCR e-paper service. Authored (opinion/analysis) articles matched to a suggested angle make the headroom: 100 x (1 - count / saturationCount) over the last windowDays. startDate is where `ocr` begins downloading.

effort._note: How much Groq or OpenAI may reason before answering, per job (default low). Luna read headlines as well with none as with low (the benchmark), so reasoning is switched off there; layout and the review need it. Putting printed columns back together reads junctions between blocks and missed most articles on low; medium found them. high is refused by Groq's request limits.

routingNoClaude._note: Used while Claude is switched off, which is the default (switch it on in Settings → Integrations). The jobs listed here go to OpenAI (GPT-5.6 Luna); every other job goes to Groq. OpenAI falls back to Groq, never to Claude.

limits._note: Daily spend cap per paid provider, from the token counts and the prices in pricing. Once reached, that provider's jobs go to Groq until the next day. Remove a line to remove its cap.

models._note: Model used for a job instead of the default (HIVEMIND_MODEL). Putting the columns of a printed article back together needs the stronger model: the default one missed column blocks and sometimes gave them to a neighbouring article. A job routed to groq ignores this.

routing._note: Which provider does each job first: groq (low cost) or claude. Claude stays the fallback. Measured on real stories: full-article reading and sentiment matched Claude's agreement with earlier readings; topic-fit verdicts agreed only 79%, so they stay on Claude.
